elements.quote: Our living systematic review (LSR) focuses on suicide prevention in relation to COVID-19
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a living systematic review.

elements.quote: Our living systematic review (LSR) focuses on suicide prevention in relation to COVID-19, with this iteration synthesising relevant evidence up to June 7 th 2020.
elements.reason: The abstract provides an explicit statement of the main objective (focus on suicide prevention in relation to COVID-19).

elements.quote: Eligibility criteria include incidence/prevalence of suicidal behaviour, exposure-outcome relationships and effects of interventions in relation to the COVID-19 pandemic. Outcomes of interest are suicide, self-harm or attempted suicide and suicidal thoughts. No restrictions are placed on language or study type, except for single-person case reports.
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the main inclusion and exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: Method: Automated daily searches feed into a web-based database with screening and data extraction functionalities. ... synthesising relevant evidence up to June 7 th 2020.
elements.reason: The abstract mentions automated daily searches and the date, but does not name specific information sources (e.g., PubMed, Scopus) in the abstract text.
The abstract does not specify the methods used to assess risk of bias in the included studies.
The abstract mentions 'synthesising relevant evidence' but does not specify the methods used to present and synthesize the results (e.g., narrative synthesis, meta-analysis).

elements.quote: Results: Searches identified 2070 articles, 29 (28 studies) met our inclusion criteria, of which 14 articles were research letters or preprints awaiting peer review.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies (28 studies) but does not report the total number of participants.

elements.quote: Results: ... No studies reported on changes in rates of suicidal behaviour. Case series were largely drawn from news reporting in low/middle income countries and factors associated with suicide included fear of infection, social isolation and economic concerns.
elements.reason: The abstract presents results for the main outcomes (suicide, self-harm, suicidal thoughts).
The review did not conduct a meta-analysis (as stated in Methods section 'callout_0': 'We have not considered it appropriate to combine any results identified so far in a meta-analysis').
The abstract does not report comparisons between groups ('No studies reported on changes in rates of suicidal behaviour').

elements.quote: Conclusions: A marked improvement in the quality of design, methods, and reporting in future studies is needed. ... However, suicide data are challenging to collect in real time and economic effects are evolving.
elements.reason: The abstract briefly summarizes important limitations of the included evidence (quality of design, data collection challenges).

elements.quote: Conclusions: ... Our LSR will provide a regular synthesis of the most up-to-date research evidence to guide public health and clinical policy to mitigate the impact of COVID-19 on suicide.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of the results and their important implications.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract does not provide the register name and registration number.

elements.quote: Given the health and economic threats posed by the pandemic to the global community, there are concerns that rates of suicide and suicidal behaviour may rise during and in its aftermath.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the current state of knowledge and uncertainties regarding suicide rates during the pandemic.

elements.quote: Our LSR will provide a regular synthesis of the most up-to-date research evidence to guide public health and clinical policy to mitigate the impact of COVID-19 on suicide.
elements.reason: The abstract explains the importance and need for the review to guide policy and mitigate impact.

elements.quote: Details of the living review method, justification for its use and our transition plan are provided in our protocol (John et al ., 2020a).
elements.reason: The need for the living review is explained, but the text cites a protocol rather than explicitly identifying and citing a previous systematic review.
The provided text does not describe the proposed mechanism of action of the interventions.
The provided text does not mention a logic model for complex interventions.

elements.quote: The overarching aim of the review is to identify and appraise any newly published evidence from around the world that assesses the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on suicide deaths, suicidal behaviours, self-harm and suicidal thoughts, or that assesses the effectiveness of strategies to reduce the risk of suicide deaths, suicidal behaviours, self-harm and suicidal thoughts, resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic.
elements.reason: The document explicitly states the overarching aim/objective in the 'Aim' section (text_6).

While the review mentions assessing the effectiveness of strategies (interventions) in text_6, the specific planned comparisons for these interventions are not explicitly stated using PICO or an appropriate variant in the provided text.

elements.quote: Study participants may be adults or children of any ethnicities living in any country. elements.quote: most of the published evidence that we identified had important limitations. Importantly, much of the literature is not yet peer reviewed so the quality of reported studies may change. There were eight research letters, five pre-prints and for many others very short timeframes between submission and acceptance. All included studies were observational in design and prone to multiple sources of bias (eg, recall bias, selection bias, confounding). No conclusions can be drawn regarding causality and temporality from cross sectional studies... The lack of baseline data in the majority of surveys included in the review and adjustments made to standardised measures to assess suicidal behaviours as well as the range of measures and timing asked made assessment of findings problematic.
